text:
amanda: quick flag - spotted a console glitch during the workspace-switch rollout, saved-search results briefly showed rows from a different workspace after the session handoff. putting screenshots in #incidents :frowning:
jorge: thanks, can you repro? steps? which build/sha?
amanda: yes repro steps: 1) login as user A in org acme, 2) toggle dev feature workspace-switch via profile -> flags (canary on), 3) open Saved Searches, 4) click ‘switch workspace’ then hit back quickly. repeats ~30% locally
priya: hmm that sounds like a stale session context being applied after the frontend sent a new workspace header. did you see any header mismatch in logs?
dan: pasted the relevant log lines:
```
WARN 2024-11-12T09:03:12Z session-handoff user=ua_42 session_claim=org-acme header_workspace=org-beta message="workspace claim mismatch"
DEBUG 2024-11-12T09:03:12Z api: req_id=xx-zz path=/api/saved-searches auth=ok token_sub=ua_42 received_x_workspace=org-beta
```
maya: that log line indicates the server accepted a request with X-Workspace-ID=org-beta but the session token is still scoped to org-acme. server should reject that by default, not merge results.
jorge: how are we currently enforcing scope? I thought frontend always passes workspace in header and server trusts token mapping + header?
priya: current flow: frontend sets X-Workspace-ID from local state, backend primarily validates token->workspace during auth but due to a race when session handoff occurs we sometimes accept header first and run the query before auth mapping finishes updating \amanda: reproduction shows a ~500ms window where header wins and DB query runs with the wrong workspace filter, so some rows from the other org leak into the UI for a split second.
dan: quick mitigation: add guard early in request pipeline to compare token.sub org claim with header and fail-fast if mismatch. I can ship a server patch in the next deploy window.
maya: +1 to server-side guard. we should never rely purely on frontend state for scoping. also add an explicit audit log entry when mismatch occurs.
jorge: small debate: do we require the frontend to stop sending X-Workspace-ID and let the server infer workspace always? removing header will be a bigger rollback for client.
priya: prefer keeping header (helps load balancing/routing) but server must canonicalize and assert mapping. header can be advisory only.
infra-bot: deploy status: canary group 2 deployed at 09:00 UTC, traffic 5% -> paused autoscaling. no rollbacks yet.
amanda: action items: (1) dan to push server guard and audit log (PR + quick canary) (2) jorge to add e2e that simulates session handoff race and asserts no cross-org rows (3) priya to add a telemetry counter and alert for header/token mismatches (4) maya to coordinate with security for incident doc if we find data exfil.
dan: will open PR now, target 2-hour canary. tagging @jorge for tests.
jorge: will add e2e and a couple unit tests for request pipeline. if server guard goes in, we should also add a defensive DB query param requiring explicit workspace=claim to avoid accidental wildcard.
priya: timeline: if PR goes in and canary looks clean, we can re-enable rollout and continue. if we see any mismatch rate >0.1% in telemetry, pause rollout and rollback canary.
maya: thanks everyone. filing an internal ticket and linking this thread. please paste PR links and telemetry dashboard here once available. :thumbsup:
